newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Some doubt PairGain takeover talk.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Some doubt PairGain takeover talk.

text.p: PairGain Technologies Inc options were busy Friday for the second-straight day as takeover rumors pushed the stock higher.
Options traders, however, said the activity lacked the full-out buying flood that typically accompanies takeover stocks.
One trader in Chicago also said trading was not straight call buying across the board, which is often the case in takeover situations.
But by about 1340 CDT/1840 GMT, PairGain shares were up 1-3/8 at 22-1/4 on more than nine million shares.
Traders cited Lucent Technologies Inc and Tikva, Israel-based ECI Telecom Ltd as possible suitors. A Lucent spokesman declined comment and PairGain officials were not available.

According to Lawrence McMillan, who publishes the Daily Volume Alert, PairGain options volume Thursday rose to more than 16,200 contracts, up from an average daily rate of about 3,350. Most of the increase was on the call side.
Call were by far the most active PairGain options again Friday, but the volume was down from Thursday's.
Trading was led by the 1,945 August 20 calls that traded.
Other busy calls included the August 22-1/2 calls and the September 25 calls, which traded 1,600 and 1,645 contracts, respectively.
The options trader said the order flow for the calls was not all on the buy side, with some investors selling calls. He said that action suggested not everyone believed the buyout talk.
An options dealer at a brokerage firm in Chicago added that the call prices were not terribly inflated relative to the volatility, which was around 80 in the August and September futures, he said.
"I looking at these calls -- the Augs and the Septs -- and relative to the historical volatility in the stock, they're not particularly expensive," he said.
He explained that typically call prices on a takeover-rumor stock's options will inflate dramatically as demand for the calls pushes premiums to out-of-line levels.

"Anytime you get an 80 volatility stock, the (call) premiums are going to be high," the dealer said. "But the premiums relative to historical volatility in the stock are in line. That's kind of unusual" for a rumored takeover.
Average volatility for PairGain is around 70.
